paper_metadata.title: Accelerating variational quantum Monte Carlo using the variational quantum eigensolver

summary: The paper introduces Quantum‑Enhanced Variational Monte Carlo (QEVMC), which uses VQE-generated samples as the initial distribution for classical VMC. For the Fermi–Hubbard model (1×4–2×4 lattices) and transverse-field Ising models (up to 80 spins), the method reduces MCMC convergence time, with simulated speedups up to ~14× for Hubbard and up to ~46× for Ising instances, though no asymptotic quantum advantage is shown.

experiments.description: Quantum-enhanced variational Monte Carlo (QEVMC) on the Fermi-Hubbard model using VQE-generated initial samples, evaluated on small instances with exact classical comparison and on larger instances using stored VQE samples.

algorithm.variant: VQE-generated samples used as the initial distribution for Metropolis-Hastings VMC (QEVMC)
algorithm.convergence_criteria: VMC chain length / target total variation distance or energy error; VQE states taken from prior experiments rather than re-optimized here

hyperparameters.VQE_layers_used_for_initial_distribution: simulated and experimental distributions from prior work; small-system comparisons include theoretical VQE and experimental VQE distributions
hyperparameters.mcmc_mixer: random walk moving a randomly chosen electron to a neighboring site
hyperparameters.samples_for_large_systems: concatenation of L/8 independent samples from 1x8 VQE distribution

algorithm.parameter_initialization: VQE samples taken from prior experimental/simulated VQE distributions; classical baseline starts from Slater determinant (U=0 ground state)

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Computational basis bitstrings represent fermion occupation configurations; VMC samples bitstrings and evaluates Gutzwiller amplitudes classically
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize energy of the Gutzwiller wavefunction for the Fermi-Hubbard Hamiltonian
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Half-filling and occupation-number postselection/error mitigation in experimental VQE data; MCMC respects particle-number-conserving moves
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H = - sum_{<i,j>,sigma}(a^†_{iσ} a_{jσ} + a^†_{jσ} a_{iσ}) + U sum_k n_{k↑} n_{k↓}

problem_instance.description: Fermi-Hubbard model on rectangular lattices, including small exact-comparison instances and larger scalability demonstrations

dataset_specification.source_of_VQE_data: experimental and simulated distributions from prior Fermi-Hubbard VQE work

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Experimental VQE data were error-mitigated by postselection on occupation number and averaging over time-reversal and reflection symmetries; larger systems used concatenated independent samples from smaller VQE distributions
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Exact stochastic-matrix-multiplication comparisons for small systems; true VMC runs for larger systems; metrics include total variation distance, local energy, energy error, and speedup factor; results shown over multiple chain lengths and 10,000 runs for some large-system plots

noise_model.noise_type: experimental VQE data with error mitigation via postselection and symmetry averaging
noise_model.error_mitigation_method: postselection on occupation number; averaging over time-reversal and reflection symmetries

implementation_details.classical_solver: Metropolis-Hastings VMC; exact stochastic matrix multiplication for small-system analysis
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Construct VQE-derived initial distributions; for large systems concatenate independent samples from 1x8 VQE distribution
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compute total variation distance, local energy, energy error, and speedup ratios

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: energy and total-variation-distance decrease with chain length; speedup depends on initial distribution

speedup_claims.conditions: simulated VQE distributions for the 1x8 Fermi-Hubbard instance; speedup measured as ratio of Metropolis chain lengths needed to reach a given total variation distance
speedup_claims.caveats: This is for exact small-system comparisons; experimental 1x8 and 2x4 cases showed little speedup.
Speedup depends on target total variation distance threshold.
Paper states there is little speedup in the 1x8 experiment overall, despite a reported speedup factor figure.
Paper states there is little speedup in the 2x4 experiment overall, despite a reported speedup factor figure.

speedup_claims.conditions: large-system VMC runs using concatenated 1x8 VQE samples
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper does not provide a single numeric speedup factor for these larger systems in text.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: VQE sample generation is offline; QEVMC uses classical MCMC with improved initialization
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Metropolis-Hastings mixing time depends on relaxation time and initial distribution; no explicit asymptotic bound for the full hybrid procedure

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not established; experiments use small lattices (1x4, 1x8, 2x4) and simulated scaling tests up to 1x48.
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Would require scalable VQE state preparation producing distributions closer to the target ground state than classical initializations for large lattices; the paper does not estimate qubit counts, circuit depth, or shot requirements.
limiting_factors: Improvement only in MCMC burn-in time (constant-factor improvement)
Small system experiments (≤16 sites) with modest speedups
Quality of VQE state determines benefit
Hybrid algorithm still dominated by classical VMC cost

notes: The paper reports experimental VQE data from prior quantum-hardware experiments on the Fermi-Hubbard model, but does not name the device/provider in this paper.

num_qubits is not explicitly stated for the VQE source circuits in the extracted text; the paper discusses 1x4, 1x8, 2x4, 1x16, 1x24, and 1x48 problem sizes, but not the exact circuit register size for the VQE preparation circuits.
The paper reports speedups in MCMC convergence (e.g., up to ~14× in simulations and ~6× with experimental VQE data) but does not claim asymptotic quantum advantage.
Speedups arise from improved initial distributions rather than algorithmic complexity improvements.

experiments.description: Quantum-enhanced variational Monte Carlo (QEVMC) on the transverse-field Ising model using VQE-generated initial samples, evaluated on 16-, 24-, 40-, and 80-spin systems and within stochastic reconfiguration optimization.

algorithm.variant: Hamiltonian variational ansatz used to generate initial samples for VMC / stochastic reconfiguration (QEVMC)
algorithm.optimizer: BFGS for VQE state preparation; stochastic reconfiguration (SR) for NQS optimization
algorithm.convergence_criteria: fixed number of VQE layers; SR run for fixed iterations; MCMC chain length chosen to reach target TVD or relative energy error

boundary_conditions: open boundary conditions for generated VQE samples
periodic boundary conditions for reference NQS from prior work in 40/80-spin comparison

algorithm.parameter_initialization: VQE starts from all-plus state; NQS SR starts from random weights; VQE layers optimized with BFGS

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Spin configurations are computational-basis bitstrings; VMC samples bitstrings and evaluates NQS amplitudes classically
problem_formulation.objective_function: Find low-energy approximation to the ground state of the transverse-field Ising Hamiltonian and use VQE samples to accelerate MCMC/SR
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: No explicit constraints beyond spin-flip sampling; VQE samples used as initial distribution
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H = -J sum_i Z_i Z_{i+1} - h sum_j X_j

problem_instance.description: 1D transverse-field Ising model at h in {0.5, 1.0, 2.0} with system sizes 16, 24, 40, and 80 spins

dataset_specification.reference_NQS_source: Carleo and Troyer 2017 for 40/80-spin approximate ground states

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: For 40/80-spin tests, 20-spin VQE samples with open boundary conditions were concatenated independently to form initial samples for larger systems
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Exact TVD and energy-error calculations for 16-spin case; energy-error trajectories for 24/40/80-spin cases; speedup measured as ratio of chain lengths needed to reach a fixed error threshold; SR optimization compared using uniform vs VQE initial distributions

noise_model.noise_type: experimental VQE data used as initial distribution; no explicit device noise model given in the paper text

implementation_details.classical_solver: Metropolis-Hastings MCMC; stochastic reconfiguration (SR) for NQS training; exact calculations for some small-system comparisons
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Generate VQE distributions with Hamiltonian variational ansatz; concatenate smaller-system samples for larger systems
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compute local energy estimates, total variation distance, relative energy error, and speedup factors

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: energy error decreases with chain length and SR iterations; VQE initialization improves convergence

speedup_claims.conditions: 16-spin TFI, h = 1, using a four-layer VQE state compared with the uniform distribution
speedup_claims.caveats: Speedup is measured in chain length needed to reach a target total variation distance or relative energy error.

speedup_claims.conditions: 24-spin TFI, h = 1, using a one-layer VQE state compared with the uniform distribution
speedup_claims.caveats: This is reported for the VMC/MCMC convergence comparison, not for the VQE optimization itself.

speedup_claims.conditions: 40-spin and 80-spin TFI comparisons using concatenated 20-spin VQE samples
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states the speedup scales up with system size, but does not provide a single numeric factor in text.

speedup_claims.conditions: 24-spin TFI during stochastic reconfiguration with 1-4 layer VQE initial distributions
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports a speedup factor plot but does not give exact numeric values in text for each layer.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: VQE sample generation is offline; QEVMC uses classical MCMC with improved initialization
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: SR with MCMC sampling; no explicit asymptotic complexity bound given

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not established; simulations evaluate systems up to 80 spins.
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Would require running VQE circuits on hardware capable of preparing useful initial distributions for large Ising systems; resource estimates are not provided.
limiting_factors: Experiments performed with simulated VQE states
Speedups depend on quality of VQE initialization
Overall algorithm dominated by classical stochastic reconfiguration and MCMC

notes: The paper reports VQE-generated experimental distributions but does not name the specific quantum hardware or provider in the extracted text.
num_qubits is inferred from the spin-system sizes and the use of VQE-generated bitstring samples, but the exact VQE circuit register size is not explicitly stated in the extracted text.
Results show speedups up to ~20× (16 spins) and ~46× (24 spins) in MCMC convergence when using VQE-derived initial distributions.
These are constant-factor improvements observed in simulation, not demonstrated quantum advantage.
